preferenceReasons: The CLI could query the supplied pre-generated analyzer directory immediately after the repository build, without installing fixture dependencies or starting a long-lived server.
CLI responses were direct JSON, which was easier to capture and inspect than MCP's SSE envelope containing string-escaped JSON.
MCP returned equivalent package totals and importer-chain evidence and is attractive for an interactive tool client, but raw HTTP use required more setup and response decoding.
Starting MCP rebuilt the fixture and selected the new snapshot by default, whereas the CLI's explicit analyze directory made the analyzed dataset easier to keep stable.

findings.evidence: query_bundle_sources grouped by package reports 939,555 raw and 351,248 compressed bytes, the largest non-framework client package on /dashboard. explain_bundle_source for one 124,288-byte language module reports an unambiguous synchronous chain language module -> highlight.js/lib/index.js -> highlight.js/es/index.js -> dashboard page; the same chain and nearly identical totals were returned by CLI and MCP.
findings.whyLikelyOptimizable: The analyzer proves the package-wide language index is synchronously reachable from the route and contributes almost a megabyte raw. Importing/registering only required language modules, or loading highlighting only when needed, should avoid shipping unrelated language implementations.

findings.evidence: Package grouping reports 192,225 raw and 64,893 compressed bytes. explain_bundle_source reports 161,700 raw and 52,935 compressed bytes for chart.js/dist/chart.js and an unambiguous synchronous importer chain through chart.js/auto/auto.js to the dashboard page.
findings.whyLikelyOptimizable: The analyzer shows the auto-registration entry is synchronously in the route. A selective Chart.js registration/import or route interaction-based dynamic loading could reduce the controllers/elements/plugins shipped initially.

findings.evidence: Package grouping reports 69,770 raw and 24,943 compressed bytes. explain_bundle_source selects lodash/lodash.js unambiguously and shows a direct synchronous edge from that full build to the dashboard page.
findings.whyLikelyOptimizable: The analyzer identifies the monolithic Lodash build as the selected source rather than smaller method modules. Per-method imports, native equivalents, or an import-optimization transform are likely to retain only used functionality.

findings.evidence: Package grouping reports 61,328 raw and 19,333 compressed bytes. explain_bundle_source selects moment/moment.js unambiguously and shows a direct synchronous edge to the dashboard page.
findings.whyLikelyOptimizable: A full date-time library is synchronously paid on the dashboard. If the route uses limited formatting, a smaller API/runtime-native formatter or deferred loading may remove most of this cost.

missedOrUnclearAreas: The analyzer establishes reachability and byte attribution, not which exports or runtime features the UI actually needs; source inspection is intentionally deferred until after this analyzer-only report exists.

The dashboard page source is reported as 30,138 client raw bytes but only 505 compressed bytes. This unusual ratio may affect parsing/build cost, but it is not a strong transfer-size opportunity and cannot be interpreted safely from analyzer data alone.
The overview's total environment includes client, server, and traced assets, so route totals are not equivalent to browser transfer. Findings therefore use the client package view.
Compressed source sizes are analyzer estimates because attributed parts are compressed independently.

The MCP startup created a newer snapshot with about 147 KB more raw bytes on every route. compare_bundles shows the increase is broad and nearly uniform; without source-based investigation it is treated as build/snapshot variance rather than an app optimization finding.
No baseline with an implemented optimization was available, so savings are upper bounds represented by current package contributions rather than measured post-change deltas.

overallAssessment: The analyzer makes a strong, evidence-backed case that /dashboard has four actionable client-side dependency costs. The standout is highlight.js, followed by Chart.js; selective imports/registration offer the largest likely wins. Lodash and Moment are smaller but still concrete synchronous costs. CLI is the more reproducible low-friction interface for scripted analysis of supplied data, while MCP exposes equivalent capabilities for integrated interactive clients.

correctHits.sourceConfirmation: The dashboard imports the top-level highlight.js entry but highlights only one JavaScript snippet. A core build plus explicit JavaScript language registration would avoid the analyzer-observed all-languages index chain.

The dashboard imports chart.js/auto and renders only one bar chart. Selectively registering the bar controller, elements, scales, and required plugins directly addresses the analyzer-observed auto-entry cost.
The dashboard imports the full default Lodash build and calls only groupBy once on a four-item static array. A per-method import or small native reduction can remove the monolithic client dependency.
The dashboard imports Moment solely for moment().format('LLLL'). Intl.DateTimeFormat or a smaller formatter can satisfy this narrow use.

misses: The analyzer-only report did not explicitly recommend shrinking the 'use client' boundary. Source shows the entire dashboard is a client component even though only Chart lifecycle/canvas behavior requires the client; splitting a small chart island from server-renderable grouping, timestamp, and highlighted markup could remove or relocate additional client work.

The analyzer-only report noted but did not turn the 30,138 raw / 505 compressed dashboard source into a finding. Source reveals this is normal concise application code in the checked-out fixture, so treating the raw attribution as an optimization would not have been useful.
groundTruthComparison.summary: All four package findings are correct and map to concrete over-broad imports or replaceable narrow uses. The main miss is architectural: the analyzer evidence showed a route-wide client entry, but the initial report stopped at package-level fixes instead of proposing a smaller client-component boundary.
